title: open-source severity pass (HPO Severity-modifier dominant-sequela join) — S lift / new order-lock

severity_hpo_excluded.exclusion_reason: modifier sits on a morphological feature (tall stature), which is not a severity-determining sequela; 'Mild tall stature' is severity-uninformative for the disease (category error). Not lifted

feature-level 'Mild' on type-I osteopenia; the cohort entity is the OI umbrella (types I-IV) spanning mild (type I) to perinatal-lethal (type II), so a single sub-type/feature modifier cannot tier the spectrum (BURDEN_INDEX spectrum rule). S kept at the [H] spectrum midpoint, not lifted

type-III osteoporosis carries a Severe grade — the OPPOSITE of the type-I 'Mild' modifier on the same umbrella entity; the contradiction is itself proof that a sub-type/feature severity is not the umbrella's disease-level tier (spectrum rule). Not lifted

the severity-graded term is on cognitive involvement, which is NOT DMD's dominant sequela (progressive motor failure and loss of ambulation is); reading 'Mild' as the disease tier would catastrophically understate a severe, life-shortening disease (category error). Not lifted

modifier on a non-dominant respiratory feature; Fabry's dominant untreated burden is renal/cardiac/cerebrovascular disease and neuropathic pain, so 'Mild airway obstruction' does not represent disease severity (category error). Not lifted

severity is encoded in the phenotype term itself (severe vertebral flattening) on a single skeletal feature; achondroplasia overall has near-normal lifespan and normal cognition (banked M=0.4 [H]), so a disease-level 'Severe' tier read from one feature would overstate it (category error). Not lifted
